To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the legs of the social insect Frieseomelittavaria are equipped with a variety of glands.
the legs of stingless bee workers have a variety of glands that are probably involved with lubrication, but the function of the remaining glands is still unknown.
we found 15 exocrine glands in the stingless bee F. varia (Le Peletier), of which six are novel for social insects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphology, histology and function of the exocrine glands in the stingless bee F. varia.
the description and functional interpretation of the glands of social insects.
the diversity of glands in the legs, and the function of these glands in social insect behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these glands have a function in lubrication and/or defense.
there is a high degree of gland diversity in social insect legs.
the legs of social insects are equipped with a variety of glandular structures, with a diversity of glandular types, and with a diversity of glandular locations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exocrine glands in the legs of F. varia workers may have a function in the maintenance of the legs and their joints, but that the function of many glands is not yet known.
the legs of social insects are not just used for locomotion, but are a rich source of chemical signals.
the leg exocrine glands of stingless bees are much more diverse than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diversity of exocrine structures in stingless bees is underestimated, and that the legs are a promising site for further research.
there is a large amount of diversity of glands in the legs, and that this diversity is probably a result of convergent evolution, as the glands are similar to those in other social Hymenoptera.
stingless bees have a more diverse set of leg exocrine glands than previously thought, and that the function of many of these glands is not yet known.
